To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dominant paradigm of video-text representation learning – noise contrastive loss – is overly-strict, forcing representations of semantically-related samples to be dissimilar, (2) we alleviate this by learning representations that are similar for semantically-related samples using a generative model, and (3) this results in representations that are better for video-to-text, text-to-video retrieval, and downstream tasks.

(i) we show that the noise contrastive learning paradigm, which has been used for video-text representation, is too strict in that it pushes away representations of semantically related samples, (ii) we propose a novel support-set bottleneck that alleviates this problem, (iii) our approach outperforms other methods on video-text retrieval.
